reasons: Status is correct: the cited Section 9 provisions are all for-cause exits (material breach, insolvency, Customer special-cause) and the surveyed sections add only non-renewal on 180 days' notice and a force-majeure exit, so no Customer termination-for-convenience right exists in a three-year committed term — walk-away territory under T4C, properly treated as a missing-clause finding.

The inserted language tracks the playbook model language closely: Customer convenience termination on 30 days' written notice with refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, plus confirmation that Vendor has no convenience right during a term (the preferred position's second limb).

Placement is sensible — appended within the Termination section immediately after the other Customer termination rights — and the edit is additive, leaving existing for-cause rights untouched (smallest edit that reaches the position).
Comment is accurate, concise, uses the required prefix and first person plural, explains the change and the three-year no-exit rationale, and offers the 60-day fallback.

Minor, non-blocking notes: the phrase 'without penalty, early-termination charge, or further liability' and the Vendor-restriction sentence go slightly beyond the model language, but both are consistent with the preferred position and do not overreach; the new text is unnumbered and could be styled as a new Section 9.6 for cleanliness.
